title: PVC cables
summary: PVC cables: thermoplastic and thermosetting forms, single core, flat twin and cpc, and flexible cables, with their sizes, uses and handling.

sections.heading: PVC forms
paragraphs: PVC comes in two main forms: thermoplastic and thermosetting.

sections.heading: PVC single core (6491X)
paragraphs: This cable comes in sizes from 1.0mm2 upwards and usually has stranded conductors, though single strand solid conductor cable is still available. It needs additional mechanical protection and is generally installed in conduit and trunking.
It is generally found in commercial, industrial and agricultural installations. A range of insulation colours are available to help identify cables.

sections.heading: Flat twin and cpc (6242Y)
paragraphs: Available from 1.0mm2 upwards. The 1.5mm2 and 2.5mm2 sizes have solid conductors and larger sizes are stranded. The sheathing gives some mechanical protection, so it can be clipped directly to a surface in less onerous conditions.
It has PVC insulated conductors and an uninsulated cpc. Flat three core and cpc (6243Y) and single core and cpc are also available. It is generally, but not exclusively, used for domestic wiring.

sections.heading: Flexible cable (3092Y and 3093Y)
paragraphs: Sizes start from 0.5mm2. Each conductor is made of many fine strands, making it much more flexible, and the sheath provides some mechanical protection. Two-core and three-core are most common but many cores are available.

It connects portable appliances to the socket outlet and connects lighting points, for example a pendant ceiling rose. Twist the strands together before termination to avoid whiskers, odd strands that miss the termination.
bullets: Twist strands before termination to avoid whiskers

sections.heading: Non-sheathed cables in conduit
paragraphs: Thermoplastic (PVC) or thermosetting insulated non-sheathed cable is covered by BS 7211 and BS 7919. It is normally used in conduit, trunking and cable ducting. Cables run in PVC conduit should not operate with a conductor temperature greater than 70°C.
bullets: Maximum 70°C conductor temperature in PVC conduit

quiz.q: Which are the two main forms of PVC?
quiz.why: PVC comes in thermoplastic and thermosetting forms.

quiz.q: Which cable is generally installed in conduit and trunking because it needs extra mechanical protection?
quiz.why: Single core cable needs additional mechanical protection and is generally installed in conduit and trunking.

quiz.q: Which cable is generally used for domestic wiring?
quiz.why: 6242Y is generally, but not exclusively, used for domestic installations.

quiz.q: What is the cpc of flat twin and cpc cable?
quiz.why: It has PVC insulated conductors and an uninsulated cpc conductor.

quiz.q: Which cable connects portable appliances to a socket outlet?
quiz.why: Flexible cable is generally used for connecting portable appliances to the socket outlet.

quiz.q: Why are strands twisted together before termination in flexible cable?
options: To avoid whiskers that miss the termination
quiz.why: Twisting ensures all strands are clamped and avoids odd strands missing the terminal.

quiz.q: Which size has solid conductors in flat twin and cpc cable?
quiz.why: 1.5mm2 and 2.5mm2 sizes have solid conductors; larger sizes are stranded.

quiz.q: What is the highest conductor temperature for cables run in PVC conduit?
quiz.why: They should not operate with a conductor temperature greater than 70°C.
